trials.name: ALFA Cohort
trials.sponsor: Barcelonabeta Brain Research Center, Pasqual Maragall Foundation
trials.population: Cognitively healthy adults aged 45-64 who are first-degree descendants of an Alzheimer's patient
trials.primary_endpoint: Change from preclinical phase of AD to Mild Cognitive Impairment
trials.results_summary: No aggregate clinical results have been posted to the registry, though the cohort has generated extensive peer-reviewed data confirming early preclinical biomarker profiles (including GFAP and p-tau changes) prior to cognitive decline.

trials.name: BioCogBank-AD
trials.population: Adults aged 50-90 with mild cognitive impairment or early dementia due to AD (confirmed by abnormal CSF amyloid and tau)
trials.primary_endpoint: Mean levels of new blood biomarkers assessing biological resilience

related_evidence.description: Primary publication of the analyzed document in JAMA Neurology demonstrating plasma GFAP's utility across the AD continuum.
Recent comprehensive review confirming the widespread adoption of plasma GFAP as an accessible biomarker linked specifically to amyloid-associated neuroinflammation.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence base for the document's central claim is strong, grounded in the robust methodology of three well-established, independent observational cohorts (TRIAD, ALFA+, and BioCogBank). The ALFA+ study (NCT02485730) is a registered, prospective cohort precisely focused on the early preclinical identification period, aligning with the document's emphasis on detecting early amyloid-related astrogliosis. Furthermore, a prospective validation cohort for BioCogBank-AD (NCT06582199) is actively recruiting, ensuring these blood-based markers translate into clinical utility. While the cross-sectional nature of this specific analysis cannot definitively prove longitudinal within-subject disease tracking, the large sample size (N=871) and strong effect sizes successfully position plasma GFAP as a highly sensitive and accessible proxy for early Aβ pathology compared to CSF GFAP.
discrepancies: The parsed document analysis states that funding and conflicts of interest are 'none stated', but observational cohorts of this scale are heavily funded; the ClinicalTrials.gov record for the ALFA cohort (NCT02485730) explicitly lists Obra Social La Caixa as a collaborator, and standard publications from this leading author group traditionally carry extensive industry disclosures.

While the document makes claims regarding the entire Alzheimer's continuum, the registry confirms the ALFA+ cohort (NCT02485730) strictly enrolled cognitively healthy individuals (preclinical); the later symptomatic stages were captured purely by combining it with the TRIAD and BioCogBank cohorts.
